title: Responsive Typography 🖋️
description: Make text scale beautifully using clamp(), rem, viewport units, and fluid type scales.

slides.title: Why Fluid Typography? 🌊
slides.content:
# Text Should Adapt, Not Jump

Fixed font sizes in `px` look fine on one screen but may be too small on mobile or too large on ultrawide. Fluid typography scales smoothly between a minimum and maximum size.

CSS provides `clamp()`, viewport units, and `calc()` to create smooth typographic scales without media queries.

slides.title: The `clamp()` Function 🔧
Fluid Heading Scale
slides.codeSnippet:
h1 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 4vw + 1rem, 4rem); }
h2 { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 3vw + 0.5rem, 2.5rem); }

quizData.question: What does `font-size: clamp(16px, 2vw, 24px);` do on a 1200px wide screen?

options.text: Sets font size to 24px because 2vw = 24px, which is the max

quizData.explanation: 2% of 1200px = 24px. The clamp's max is 24px, so it stays at 24px.

slides.title: Viewport Units for Text: `vw` 📏
slides.content:
# Directly Scale with Screen Width

- `1vw` = 1% of viewport width.
- `1vh` = 1% of viewport height.
- `vmin` = smaller of vw/vh, `vmax` = larger.

```css
.hero-title {
  font-size: 8vw; /* 8% of screen width */
}
```
But `vw` alone can get too big or small. Combine with `clamp()` or `calc()` to keep it readable.

slides.title: The Golden Rule: Use `rem` for Body Text 📖
slides.content:
# Let the User's Preferences Win

Setting `body { font-size: 100%; }` (browser default, usually 16px) and using `rem` for all other sizes respects the user's base font size setting. This is crucial for accessibility.

```css
html { font-size: 100%; }  /* or 16px */
p { font-size: 1rem; }      /* 16px */
h2 { font-size: 2rem; }     /* 32px */
```
Avoid setting `font-size` on `html` in pixels unless you have a good reason.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Fluid Type Scales Without Media Queries

Use `clamp()` with a mix of `rem` and `vw` to create an entire type scale that adapts from phone to desktop seamlessly. Tools like Utopia.fyi can generate the values for you.
